q1_issues.issue: (Patient (sk_compose $x) $x) gives the molecule the Patient role, but "is composed of" is a stative constitution predicate that creates, destroys, consumes or physically changes nothing, so the object test — and its "when unclear, default to Theme" fallback — yields Theme.

q2_gaps: constitutive "N of <mass>" NPs ("molecule of water") — the of-phrase rules enumerate possessive, partitive "of the", measure ("a cup of water") and about-phrases, and explicitly exclude the measure case from the Possession/PartOf mapping without saying what replaces it; nothing licenses re-ordering it into the compound kind water_molecule

"be composed of / consist of / be made up of" — a constitution predicate whose of-complement is not a by-phrase, so the passive rule ("a by-phrase takes the role the active subject would have had") does not determine the constituents' role

per-member distribution for a counted plural ("two hydrogen atoms", each attached to the oxygen atom) when it sits inside a universal rule: Cardinality mandates an added per-member Implication over PartOf, but there is no form for nesting an Implication inside a rule's consequent
notes: The ∀-plus-number machinery is otherwise applied correctly — Skolem-function event and Skolem group per binding, GroupOf + Cardinality on the group, QuantifierPhrase companion, compound genus for hydrogen_atom/oxygen_atom with the noun modifiers left unexposed, and the participial post-modifier "attached to" expanded as a reduced relative rather than a coined head.
